summary: A determinate or indeterminate measure of work, with the name of the work attached. Omitting `value` is what makes it indeterminate.
useWhen: work reports a fraction complete — an upload, an import, a multi-step job
work will become measurable but is not yet, and the bar should not remount when it does
a quota or usage figure is better read as a bar than a number

useInstead.when: the wait is short and unmeasurable
useInstead.why: an indeterminate bar occupies a block of layout to say what a spinner says inline

useInstead.when: the region is being replaced by content

success.use: work that finished, where the bar stays on screen as a record

warning.note: warning describes the VALUE, not a failure of the bar

error.use: a quota exceeded, or a job that failed part-way
error.note: the bar is still reporting correctly — reserve this for the measured thing being bad

sm.use: inside a row or a dense table cell

requires: `label` — it is required, because role="progressbar" announces a number and a number with no noun sounds like information while carrying none
`valueText` when a percentage is not what a person wants read aloud — "3 of 12 files"
notes: indeterminate omits aria-valuenow entirely, as the ARIA spec asks; a bar reporting aria-valuenow=0 forever says the work is stuck rather than unmeasured
value is clamped to 0..max, so a caller cannot render a bar past its own end

antiPatterns.dont: <ProgressBar label="Loading" value={0} /> while the total is unknown
antiPatterns.why: value={0} announces "0 percent" indefinitely. Omitting value is how you say "not measurable yet"

antiPatterns.dont: swapping a Spinner for a ProgressBar once the size is known
antiPatterns.do: one ProgressBar, with `value` appearing when it becomes known
antiPatterns.why: the swap remounts the node and takes the live region with it, so the transition is silent to a screen reader

antiPatterns.do: leave the bar and put the failure in an Alert
antiPatterns.why: intent describes the value being measured. A failed request is not a red measurement, it is a different message
